children: rose 7.73% in premarket trading after the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Paramount is closing in on a settlement over the antitrust suit that's blocked its $111 billion WBD acquisition since July.

Paramount is racing the clock. Starting at the end of September, it owes WBD shareholders $7 million a day, roughly $650 million a quarter, for every day the deal stays stalled. Paramount has also floated relocating its headquarters out of California, widely read as leverage against California attorney-general Rob Bonta. On remedies, Paramount has offered to keep releasing 30 films a year in theaters, but Bonta has pushed back in favor of structural changes such as asset sales.

The deal would hand Paramount CEO David Ellison control of CNN, TBS, HBO Max and the DC Comics and Harry Potter franchises. It's already cleared antitrust review in nearly 70 jurisdictions, including the UK and Mexico, and the FCC approved the Middle Eastern sovereign funds' 49.5% stake this week. A trial is set for March 2027 if talks fail. Paramount and Bonta's office both declined to comment.

title: Paramount Stock Jumps 7% on WBD Settlement Talks
